FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standard. Institution on 21 February 1986, after the draft finalized by the Nutrition Sectional Committee had been approved by the Agricultural and Food Products Divilion Council. 0.2 Protein forms an essential constituent of human diet. Cottonseed oilcakel are now increasingly used for the preparation of edible cottonseed flour and there is considerable scope for commercial production of this product. The flour, is rich in protein and lysine and may be used .a a protein supplement in human dietaries. It is obtained as a powder which may be used both in blended and processed foods, In view of these possibilities, the Regional Research Laboratory, Hyderabad, carried out pioneering work on the production of edible cottonseed flour made by the liquid cyclone precess and it is now being manufactured in the country on a commercial scale. This standard has been prepared to help in exercising proper quality control of edible cottonseed flour, made by the liquid cyclone process (LCP) from eottenseed meals. 0.3 A separate Indian Standard ( IS : 4876-1986* ) has been published on edible cottonseed flour ( solvent extracted).

0.4 While formulating this standard due consideration has been given to
the relevant rules i�� ued by the Government of India: under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. This standard ~J however, subject to the restrictions imposed under thaf Act, wherever applicable.

.

purchaser and the supplier.

1. SCOPE
1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of sampling and test for edible cottonseed flour prepared by liquid cyclone process.
2. REQ,UlREMENTS 2.1 DescriptioD - The material shall be obtained from cleaned, delinted and dehulled cottonseeds by means of liquid cyclone process. It shall be in the form of flour of white to pale brownish-yellow colour, uniform in composition and free from insects, rodent hair and excreta, fungal infection, objectionable odour and rancid taste. It shall not contain added flavouring or odouring agents or any other extraneoul matter.
NOTE- The appearance. talte and odour .hall be determined by organoleptic testl.

2.2 Particle Size - Unless otherwise specified by the purchaser, the material shall be such that it passes completely through a 150-micron IS Sieve [ see IS : 460 ( Part 1 )-1978f ].

2 3 The material shall be manufactured, packed, stored and distributed under hygienic conditions in licensed premises (SI' IS : 2491-1972:).
2.~

The material shall allo comply with the requirements given in Table 1.

3. PACKING
3.1 The material shall be packed in sealed metal containers or jutel hessian bags with polyethylene lining of 40 to 75 microns.

4. MARKING t.l The follow-ing particulars shall be marked legibly or labelled on each container:
a) Name of the material;

b) Name and address of the manufacturer;
c) Batch or code number; d) Net mass; e) Date of manufacture; and
f) Any other requirements under the Standards of Weights and Measures (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 1977.

t.1.1 Each container may also be marked with the lSI Certification Mark.
NOTB - The use of the lSI Certification Mark is governed by the proviaioDi of the Indian Standarda Institution (Certification Marks) Act and the Rules and RegulatioDi made thereunder. The lSI Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard convey. the Ulurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of iDapectioD, testin, and quality control which is devised and supervised by lSI and operated by the producer. lSI Marked products are allo continuously checked by lSI for conformity to that standard u a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which. licence for the use oC the lSI Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or proceuora. may be obtained from the Indian Standard. Iaatitutioll.

5.3 The lot shall be declared aa conforming to the requirement. of the Ipecification if all the telt results on the test sample, for moisture determination and sample for microbiological requirements are found to be conforming to the relevant specification requirements.
